notes: The breadboard in the image labels the half nearest the power rails at the bottom as rows a-e and the upper half as f-j. I followed the catalogue naming: bank 't' = rows a-e (the lower half in the image) and bank 'b' = rows f-j (the upper half). The rails next to the a-e half (the lower rails in the image) are named tp (+) and tn (-).
Exact rail hole numbers (tp.1, tp.3, tn.1, tn.7) are estimated from the image. Any hole on the same rail is electrically equivalent.

The button straddles the centre gap in columns 4 and 6. I assumed the legs in one column are the internally joined pair. Side 1 is column 4, which goes to 5V through the orange wire. Side 2 is column 6, which goes to pin 2 and to the pull-down resistor.
The resistor is a 10k pull-down, stored as value=10000. It runs from column 6 (the pin 2 and button side 2 node) to column 9, and a black wire takes column 9 to the GND rail.
The red wire goes from 5V to the + rail. The black wire goes from the second GND pin (GND.2) to the - rail.
The LED on pin 13 is the board's built-in LED, so it is not a separate part.
